original_question: In the rank-one case, let J be a division Jordan algebra and let St(J) denote the rank-one Steinberg group defined in this section. Is St(J) centrally closed for every such J except the finite fields F_q with q in {2, 3, 4, 9}?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1: the paper's rank-one central-closure conjecture for the Steinberg group attached to a quadratic Jordan division algebra.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the main mathematical content of the paper's target statement: it is about the rank-one Steinberg group St(J), asks for central closedness, quantifies over all Jordan-division inputs J, and singles out exactly the four exceptional finite-field cases F_2, F_3, F_4, and F_9.
missing_details: The paper's hypothesis is not merely 'division Jordan algebra' in loose language, but the paper-faithful notion of a quadratic Jordan division algebra J.
The question should make explicit that St(J) is the rank-one Steinberg group attached to J in the paper's sense, rather than an arbitrary group denoted St(J).
The four exceptions should be stated as isomorphism types of J as Jordan algebras: J ≅ F_q with q in {2,3,4,9}.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should not say 'defined in this section'; it should identify St(J) intrinsically as the paper's rank-one Steinberg group associated with J.
If one wants the paper's exact intent, the formulation should stay at the conjectural level of Conjecture 1.1 and not silently broaden to neighboring rank-one or Moufang-set variants.
refined_question: Let J be a quadratic Jordan division algebra, and let St(J) denote the rank-one Steinberg group associated with J in the sense of the paper. Is St(J) centrally closed for every such J, with the only exceptions the cases J ≅ F_q for q ∈ {2,3,4,9}?
justification: Your draft is already very close to the paper's intended open problem. The main correction is terminological and structural: the paper's conjecture is formulated for quadratic Jordan division algebras, and the question should identify St(J) as the paper's rank-one Steinberg group attached to J rather than by a local phrase like 'defined in this section'. The introduction is the right place to anchor the formulation, and Conjecture 1.1 is the nearest official statement. Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 are part of the same introductory discussion and should be consulted for the precise surrounding scope and evidence, but they do not justify broadening the question beyond the conjecture itself.
